subject: Tradeoff analysis: units-per-$ checks for MAP & eval
messages:
From: Amir Rao <amir@plateaumed.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unit economics checkpoint and MAP milestones before procurement

Hi Markus / Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is asking us for a short mutual action plan that includes the evaluation milestones and specific economics checks they can sign off on (tokens/$ sensitivity, caching/batching assumptions, and expected per-session token footprints). Can you send a compact checklist or playbook we can include in the MSA appendix?

Ideal timeline from our side: SOC2 evidence + MAP and econ acceptance by 2027-09-10 so we can close in September. FinOps (John) wants thresholds we can use to trigger a Dedicated capacity discussion.

I attached a brief scope doc to help.

Thanks — Amir
Head of Platform Partnerships
PlateauMed
Attachment: plateaumed_initial_scope.pdf (pdf)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Rao <amir@plateaumed.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unit economics checkpoint and MAP milestones before procurement

Amir —

Appreciate the clarity on timeline. Below is a compact, actionable set of unit-econ checks and corresponding MAP milestones we typically include for buyers who need procurement sign-off. I'll also attach a starting spreadsheet (unit-econ-scenarios-v1.xlsx) with scenarios you can run against your traffic profile.

Unit-econ checklist (acceptance items for MAP):
- Baseline tokens/request and tokens/session: define a 95p request size and 95p session length from sample traffic (we recommend sending 500 sample sessions).
- Tokens/$ sensitivity: run three cost scenarios (p50/p75/p95) showing tokens per USD with current model selection and with 8-bit quantized variant.
- Caching assumptions: prefix caching and per-session KV cache expected hit rate (we model +30% cost reduction at 65% prefix-hit). Provide sample TTLs and invalidation rules.
- Batching strategy: expected batching window (10–50ms) and throughput targets; show latency impact vs cost (tokens/$).
- Fallback plan: define fallback model variant (smaller quantized model) with acceptance criteria for quality delta (e.g., rouge/accuracy regression <4%).
- Acceptance gates: pass/fail for acceptance (e.g., tokens/$ below X in p75, avg latency <200ms tail, model quality within threshold).

MAP milestones / timeline (suggested):
- Day 0: MAP kick (sample traffic + SOC2 evidence requested)
- Day 3–5: Redwood returns unit-econ scenarios + recommended configuration (batching/cache/quantization)
- Day 6–10: PlateauMed runs 3-day eval (production-like traffic replay) against pass/fail criteria
- Day 11: Validation readout, signoff or remediation plan

I'll populate the spreadsheet with default values and a few sensitivity scenarios this afternoon. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min walk-through for John and procurement next week.

— Markus
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
Attachment: unit-econ-scenarios-v1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Amir Rao <amir@plateaumed.io>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Ellis <j.ellis@plateaumed.io>
Date: 2027-08-30T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unit economics checkpoint and MAP milestones before procurement

Amir — adding procurement gate details from our side so the MAP can be explicit on acceptance criteria and what triggers a Dedicated conversation.

Procurement gating items we recommend including in the MAP: 
- Unit-econ dashboard snapshot (tokens/$) captured at t0 (redwood will provide screenshot/CSV).
- A three-scenario commit threshold: < $0.10 per 1k tokens p50 (pilot), < $0.08 per 1k tokens p75 (production target), Dedicated if p95 traffic or costs exceed agreed threshold for 14 consecutive days.
- Data handling appendix: retention window for KV cache, encryption at rest, and logging retention for audit (SOC2 artifact links to be provided).
- Remediation SLA: if cost deviance >15% versus model in MAP, trigger joint cost remediation plan (prefetch, stronger caching, or quantization).

If you want exact wording for the MSA appendix, I can draft it and circulate.

— Kimberly
Director, Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Amir Rao <amir@plateaumed.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-31T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unit economics checkpoint and MAP milestones before procurement

Quick note on the evaluation plan / pass criteria to make the MAP operational for your team.

Eval plan bullets (what we run during Day 6–10 replay):
- Traffic replay: 72-hour continuous replay of sampled production traffic at scaled volumes (x0.5 / x1 / x2) to expose tail behaviors.
- Metric sheet: tokens per request, tokens per session, avg latency (p50/p90/p99), token cache hit rate, model quality metrics pre-defined per use case (e.g., FAQ retrieval accuracy / end-to-end conversion).
- Quality regression guardrails: automated spot-checking by Redwood eval harness (10% of sessions manually labeled from sample) — regressions >4% cause remediation.
- Cost sensitivity sweep: simulate increased session lengths and caching-hit drops (-20%) to show breakpoints where units/$ degrade and to identify switch points for quantization or Dedicated triggers.

We'll upload a default runbook into the Drive folder (link above) and can tailor thresholds for PlateauMed use cases.

— Jordan
Product Manager, Inference Economics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amir Rao <amir@plateaumed.io>
Date: 2027-09-01T10:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unit economics checkpoint and MAP milestones before procurement

Adding one operational note: if PlateauMed expects bursty traffic (e.g., tfa days), we recommend a temporary burst policy in the MAP rather than immediate Dedicated commits. Typical language: 
- Burst allowance: up to 30% above committed throughput for 14 days once per quarter without penalty; beyond that, trigger Dedicated sizing evaluation.

Also: Dedicated pricing starts to make sense when sustained monthly tokens exceed ~1.2B with our current model family — we can model the exact threshold in the spreadsheet.

— Ben
Head of Platform Sales, Redwood Inference
